accuracy.evidence: Facts checked against NASA Science 'Star Basics' and 'Stars' pages, ESA 'Life cycle of stars', and the AQA GCSE Physics specification 4.8.1.2. Stars form in nebulae under gravity. Fusion of hydrogen into helium starts at about 15 million °C, the Sun's core temperature. The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old with a main-sequence life of about 10 billion years. Lifetime falls steeply with mass (roughly M^-2.5), giving about 30 million years for 10 solar masses. Stars under about 8 solar masses become red giants and then white dwarfs; heavier stars become red supergiants, explode as supernovae and leave neutron stars or black holes. Betelgeuse as a red supergiant in Orion's shoulder was checked against NASA/ESA. The numeric items 10−a, m−8, t/2 and t−u were checked at all corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented astronomy misconceptions (Bailey et al. 2009, 'Students' misconceptions about stars'; Agan 2004). That stars burn like fire is the step 0 prediction and challenge tag fire. That more fuel means a longer life is the step 2 prediction, tag fuel and m5. That all stars, the Sun included, end in supernovae is the step 4 prediction, tag heavy and m1. That a star is born in a black hole is tag end. Confusion with reflected light (planets) is tag reflect. Each wrong card in the endings step gets its own message, for example 'The Sun is not heavy enough for that'.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstarlife models this topic's own processes. Gravity squeezes a nebula through rising core temperatures until fusion starts, a hydrogen/helium gauge runs the Sun's clock to 10 billion years, three stars are ranked by lifetime, the two ending paths are built card by card, and six stars are sorted by mass across the 8-solar-mass threshold. It differs from The Sun is a star (flagstar: distance, size, what makes light) and Sun, Moon and stars (flagmoonph: daily and monthly sky patterns). The lab_distinct gate passes it under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each squeeze raises the core temperature (1, 4, 10 then 15 million °C) until 'fusion! a star is born', so the learner sees heat come from gravity, not fire. The fuel gauge turns hydrogen into helium as the Sun's age moves on, and at 4 billion years it says the Sun is about halfway. Tapping the blue giant first gets 'most fuel but burns it fastest'. Putting a supernova after the Sun gets 'not heavy enough'. Sorting 1 Sun as a supernova gets 'lighter than 8 Suns… fades as a white dwarf'.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves. 'It catches fire, like a bonfire' fails when only gravity's squeezing reaches the fusion temperature. 'Yes: more fuel, longer life' fails when the ranking only accepts the red dwarf first and the blue giant last (30 million years). 'Yes: every star explodes' for the Sun fails when the endings step rejects supernova for the Sun and the mass sort files 1 Sun under white dwarf.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; every wrong option has a tagged message naming the slip. fire: stars are not on fire, they fuse. reflect: planets reflect, stars make light. fuel: big stars burn faster. same: lifetimes range from millions to hundreds of billions of years. heavy: only stars over about 8 Suns explode. light: white dwarfs come from lighter stars. forever: the Sun's hydrogen runs out in about 5 billion years. end and planet: stars start in clouds of gas and dust.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the learner limits: kid text Flesch-Kincaid 2.6 (limit 6.5) and adult 6.9 (limit 9.5). The precise terms nebula, fusion, hydrogen, helium, red giant, white dwarf, red supergiant, supernova, neutron star and black hole are each introduced in a short sentence. Lab step texts are two or three short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step does one job (birth, fuel, lifetime against mass, endings, the mass threshold). Feedback gives the specific reason with the number involved (15 million °C, 10 billion years, 8 Suns, 30 million years), and every item explanation states the fact in one or two sentences.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px touch in light and dark were taken for every step before and after Show me. The space canvas is the same in both themes, with white and pale text on navy. The three star cards are about 110 px wide tap targets and the ending cards are two-column 32–38 px chips. After the first screenshots the ending cards were moved up so the feedback strip no longer covers the last card, the gauge labels were moved inside each colour band, and the duplicate lifespan text that overlapped the ranked list was removed.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button: 'Let gravity pull', '+2 billion years', each star (aria-label says it lives longest of those left), each of the five stage cards (aria-label 'Next stage: …') and 'white dwarf / supernova' labelled with the star's mass. The canvas aria-label reads the temperature, age, ranking or stage and the last feedback after every move. Challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors.
